minimal_optional_ROOT_observer.budget: One QA/one runtime/exact POST, short declared window, e.g.32 adjacent matching requests with at most4 selected lifecycle/fence events each. This is a proposed bounded cap, not permission to run; no generic all-runtime capture or4096 expansion.
minimal_optional_ROOT_observer.lock_release_limit: QueryEnd records successful fence acquisition bounds, not release. CommitEnd is client acknowledgement and not exact PostgreSQL release time. Record Commit/Rollback dispatch plus both PIDs/TxStatus; if unique physical holder proof is needed ROOT must collect a permitted same-DB lock/xact witness or a deterministic borrowed-Tx barrier. No SQL probe is performed here.
minimal_optional_ROOT_observer.order_limit: If R4 has already acquired that user SHARE, a later user UPDATE must wait/fail rather than retroactively invalidate the read. A new claim transaction can affect a later/current R4 acquisition. HTTP end timestamps cannot establish that lock ordering.
minimal_optional_ROOT_observer.decision: No claim-fence weakening. First prove whether the target foreground request failed at a real user fence, got cancelled/superseded, or another path failed; classify actual due-reclaim vs empty/selected claim before considering a narrowly owned behavior change.
